conviction_note: Eight small, mostly offsetting findings: a mechanical Q3 EPS drag from the second AT1 coupon and the fee normalisation management itself flagged, against a likely loan-growth guidance raise (YTD growth already above the full-year range) and a Fed hike that helps an asset-sensitive short book. The Braskem-like Stage 3 client and Argentina stress add small credit-tail negatives. The bar is unsourced, so every finding is capped small. Findings sum to -0.2 and the scaled number is -0.06 (p_up 49 x abs 2.8). The two agree on sign and differ in size because p_up absorbs the unsourced bar and this name's damped reactions.
bar: Unsourced. No Q3 2026 consensus EPS could be found (Zacks bot-blocked; MarketBeat https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/BLX/earnings/ and EarningsWhispers carry none). The only company bar is the full-year 2026 guidance reaffirmed on the Q2 call (https://wcpac01.bladex.com/uiodrupalfiles/2026-07/Q2%202026%20Transcript%20Bladex_0.pdf, 2026-07-28): commercial portfolio and average deposit growth 13-15%, NIM ~2.30%, efficiency 27-28%, adjusted ROE 14-15%, Tier 1 15-16%. 1H26 adjusted ROE was 15.3%, so the guide implies 2H adjusted ROE of roughly 12.7-14.7%. My own Q3 estimate is net profit ~$59-64M against Q2's $66.5M record; print_vs_bar_pct (+1) is measured against that guide-implied 2H run rate, not against a street number. Every size on this name is capped small for this reason.
positioning_check: Short interest about 382K shares, ~1.0% of float, 2.4 days to cover, falling 26.5% m/m (Equibles snapshot 2026-08-20, https://equibles.com/stocks/blx/short-interest). FINRA 2026-06-30: ~582.8K shares, 2.04 days (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/blx/). Not a crowded short. No usable option chain: 23 contracts open interest, no two-sided ATM legs, no skew (baseline). Stock 53.68, -2.35% over 20d, -1.97% over 5d, 14.5% below its 52-week high, 20d realised vol 18.2% annualised.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 EPS carries the second semi-annual coupon on the $200M 7.50% AT1 notes issued in September 2025 (about $7.5M, ~$0.20 a share). This is the first Q3 to carry it. Q1 2026 EPS was $1.31 on $56.4M of net profit ($1.54 before the coupon), and the company says Q1 EPS 'reflect[s] the deduction of the AT1 coupon distribution'. Q2 EPS was $1.77 on $66.5M. If aggregator estimates run Q2's $1.77 forward, headline EPS will print well below them even with flat net profit. Year-ago Q3 2025 EPS was $1.48 with no coupon.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 was the first print with the coupon (EPS -13% q/q, -7% y/y, released 2026-04-27 amc). I could not find its next-day reaction. The baseline's reaction history is cadence-implausible; the only confirmed earnings reaction in it is Q2 2026 (2026-07-27 amc), +1.08%.
findings.why_not_priced: Automated EPS snapshots (AP/Zacks) report headline EPS against a Zacks number. If that number had absorbed the coupon, a Q3 estimate below Q2's $1.77 would be visible somewhere; none is published. The analysts who cover the name (Santander, BTG, Bancolombia) model net profit and will look through it, so this matters only for the headline and is mostly a headline-only risk.
findings.independence: AT1 terms (7.50%, $200M, priced September 2025): https://bladex.com/en/Bladex-Successfully-Launches-Inaugural-US%24200-Million-AT1-Notes-Offering. The payment frequency is not stated there. The semi-annual March/September timing is inferred from the Q1 vs Q2 EPS deductions (~$8M in Q1, ~$2M in Q2).

findings.finding: Q2 fees and non-interest income ($25.6M, +86% q/q, with $7.9M of upfront structuring and syndication fees from a record 7 deals) were flagged as exceptional. The CEO said 'I do not advise to simply multiply for the rest of the year because of the syndication part'. A Q3 fee line nearer the $13-20M range would take net profit below Q2's $66.5M record.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's record fee quarter bought +1.08% (baseline, 2026-07-27 amc). No sourced reaction to a fee shortfall quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: management told the market to expect it. It is filed because a sequential profit decline will be the headline, and a thin, low-vol name can still react to the headline. If the market had fully absorbed it, the stock would not be trading near Q2-record multiples. It is 14.5% off its high, which suggests some of this is already in.
findings.independence: Same transcript as the guidance and expense findings. The Q2 release (https://www.webull.com/news/15301401715418112) shows fees and commissions up from $13.1M to $23.3M q/q.

findings.finding: The commercial portfolio was already up 17% since year-end at June 30 ($13.0B, +8% q/q) against a full-year guide of 13-15% growth. Asked why the guide was not raised, the CEO said 'there might be upside in our guidance of loan growth, but we're not ready to say that yet' and that they were 'retaining the guidance until we have better visibility on the second half'. Q3 is the natural point to raise it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced prior guidance-raise reaction for BLX. The Q2 reaffirmation with record results bought +1.08%.
findings.why_not_priced: The hint was public (BTG and Santander asked about it on the call), so part is priced. But the stock has drifted -2.35% over 20 days and sits 14.5% off its high, which is not the tape of a market already paying for a guidance raise. A raised portfolio guide plus a firmed ROE guide on the call would be new.
findings.independence: Same transcript. The Q2 release balance sheet independently shows +20% y/y commercial portfolio and +22% y/y deposits: https://www.webull.com/news/15301401715418112. The MXN 5.0B Cebures of September 2026 funds continued growth (see the financing finding).

findings.finding: The Fed raised the funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16. On the Q2 call the CEO had expected rates 'to remain stable for longer'. Bladex's book is ~65-70% due within 12 months and largely floating, so it reprices quickly. The hike lands only in the last two weeks of Q3, but it supports the ~2.30% NIM guide (1H 2.29%, Q2 2.24% and falling) and the Q4 outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced BLX reaction to a NIM-guide change. Q2's 10bp NIM decline came with a +1.08% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The macro fact is public. Its transmission to Bladex's NIM is an inference: management has not commented since the hike and no analyst preview could be found. A market that had priced a NIM upgrade would not have left the stock drifting lower since the hike.
findings.independence: Proxy, not company-confirmed. The maturity profile (~65% within 12 months, '70% of our commercial book maturing in less than a year') is from the Q2 transcript. Pre-hike, a September hike was priced at ~30% (https://www.regardsofwallstreet.com/news/september-2026-fed-meeting-dates-hike-odds), so the hike itself was partly a surprise.

findings.finding: Q2 Stage 3 rose to $75M (0.5%) from migrating 'a single client in the petrochemical sector in Brazil'. Bladex sold the bilateral loan but kept a reserved deferred-payment letter of credit, and reserve coverage fell to 1.25x. Management targets 1.5-1.6x by year-end, which requires a reserve build. Braskem, which fits that description, was cut to RD by Fitch on 2026-08-14 and filed for extrajudicial recovery on 2026-08-24 on about US$10.9B of unsecured debt. The plan offers no principal haircut, five extra years and 30 months without interest, so a further specific provision on the residual LC is possible in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 carried the first Stage 3 migration and provisions doubled to $8.6M, and the stock still rose +1.08%, so this name's holders have looked through a single-name migration once.
findings.why_not_priced: Bladex never named the client, and no source ties Bladex to the Braskem filing; I found only an old GTR note naming it a lead arranger on a Braskem supplier facility. If the market had linked them, a Braskem-driven provision would be discussed in previews, and none exist. The coverage build itself is guided, which caps the surprise.
findings.independence: Q2 transcript (client description, reserve and coverage target): https://wcpac01.bladex.com/uiodrupalfiles/2026-07/Q2%202026%20Transcript%20Bladex_0.pdf. Old Braskem-Bladex link: https://www.gtreview.com/?p=14934 (undated). The identification is an inference.

findings.finding: Q2 portfolio growth was led by Panama and Argentina (Argentine exposure mainly oil and gas and short-term gas imports). From August to October Argentine sovereign dollar bonds were the worst emerging-market performers: yields near 12%, spreads at their widest in more than a year, and the Merval down more than 10% in September. This risks Stage 2 migration, a Stage 1 provision build or a defensive call tone on a newly enlarged country exposure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced BLX reaction to a country-risk provision.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a macro-to-company proxy. Bladex's Argentine exposure size is not disclosed in the release (no country is above 14%), and its trade lending is short-tenor, which limits damage. The stock's 20-day drift of -2.35% may already reflect LatAm risk-off.
findings.independence: Q2 transcript names Argentina as a growth driver: https://wcpac01.bladex.com/uiodrupalfiles/2026-07/Q2%202026%20Transcript%20Bladex_0.pdf. Proxy, not company-confirmed.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-08 Bladex placed MXN 5.0B of three-year Cebures at TIIE de Fondeo +58bp, 1.56x covered and rated AAA local by S&P and Fitch. This is funding for a portfolio growing 20% y/y, not distress: the money buys balance-sheet growth that the Q2 numbers corroborate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced reaction. The April 2026 Cebures (MXN 4.27B) preceded a record Q2.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and small. It is filed because it corroborates the growth finding and deposit and funding diversification. It would not move the stock alone.
findings.independence: The Q2 release shows deposits +22% y/y and a commercial portfolio +20% y/y: https://www.webull.com/news/15301401715418112

findings.finding: Management guided expenses up in the second half ('expense execution is seasonally weighted towards the second half') and the efficiency ratio to 27-28% for the year, against 24.1% in Q2 and 25.2% in 1H. That implies a step-up in Q3/Q4 opex from Q2's $23.8M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced reaction. Opex +14% y/y in Q2 came with a +1.08% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it sits inside guidance the company gave. It is filed so a judge sees that the Q3 cost line was pre-announced.
findings.independence: Same transcript as the fee and guidance findings. Counts once with them as one document.

outside_window.finding: Braskem Chapter 15 recognition hearing scheduled to run to 2026-12-08. Creditor treatment of bank LC exposure is not final before then.
Next FOMC decision 2026-10-28, after the exit window closes on 2026-10-27; a further hike would add to NIM tailwind in Q4.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The mild 20-day drift (-2.35%) and the 14.5% gap to the 52-week high fit the small negatives (fee normalisation, Argentina, credit tail) already being partly priced. That leaves the guidance raise as the one item that cuts against the tape, and the net lean is near flat.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (unsourced bar): capped the AT1 EPS-headline finding from -0.4 to -0.3, because it depends entirely on what aggregators model.
Rule 6 / core table (inside guidance): fee normalisation -0.3 to -0.2 and the expense step-up -0.2 to -0.1. Both were pre-announced by management.
Rule 5 (proxy / inference): Fed-hike NIM transmission +0.4 to +0.3; Braskem identification -0.4 to -0.3, also because the coverage build is guided; Argentina -0.3 to -0.2.
Guidance-raise finding +0.6 to +0.5, because the hint was public on the call (partly priced). It stays the largest item because it lands on the guidance line.
Rule 4 (financing): Cebures kept at +0.1 after asking what the money buys (20% y/y portfolio growth).
Rule 1 / last lesson (wrong-event history): p_up moved from 48 to 49 and abs_move left at 2.8; the baseline history was discarded except the confirmed 2026-07-27 print.
